message.content:
Add **LVM pooling of multiple blank volumes** to the Nxeon migration engine (/opt/nxeon), so a customer who attaches several block-storage volumes gets their combined capacity instead of only the largest one.

## Why
Today the engine picks the single largest attached-but-unformatted disk, formats it ext4, and relocates `/var/lib/docker` + `/var/lib/containerd` onto it. A real customer attached 20 GB + 30 GB = 50 GB and the migration still refused, because 34.5 GB of Docker images didn't fit on either disk individually. Two disks are two filesystems — they don't pool by themselves. The fix is to build an LVM volume group across all blank disks and put one filesystem on top.

## Study first (do NOT run git or `npm run build`)
- `worker/migrate-real.ts` — the existing blank-disk detection (search `lsblk -b -P`, `PKNAME`, `blkid`, `EXTRA_DISK_MOUNT`) and the format/mount/relocate routine that moves BOTH container stores onto the extra disk via bind mounts + fstab. Your work replaces/extends the "pick one disk" part; keep everything downstream (relocation, bind mounts, fstab, rollback) intact.
- `lib/actions-migrate.ts` — `targetDiskFree()` returns `TargetInfo.spareDiskBytes` (currently the LARGEST blank disk) used by the wizard's storage panel.
- `components/customer/MigrationWizard.tsx` — the storage panel: `spare`, `rootAvail`, and the split-destination fit model (files→root, Docker→spare).

## Implement
1. **Detect ALL blank disks**, not just the largest. A disk qualifies ONLY if: `TYPE=disk`, no FSTYPE on itself, **no partitions/children**, no mountpoint anywhere in its tree, it is not the parent of the root filesystem, and `blkid` finds **no signature at all**. This safety bar is non-negotiable — never touch a disk that might hold data.
2. **Pool them:**
   - 0 blank disks → unchanged (everything stays on root).
   - 1 blank disk → keep today's simple path (`mkfs.ext4` directly on the disk). Do NOT introduce LVM where it isn't needed.
   - 2+ blank disks → ensure `lvm2` is installed (add to the existing package allowlist), then `pvcreate` each disk, `vgcreate nxeondata <disks...>`, `lvcreate -l 100%FREE -n data nxeondata`, `mkfs.ext4 /dev/nxeondata/data`, mount at the existing `EXTRA_DISK_MOUNT`, and persist in `/etc/fstab` **by UUID** with `nofail` so a missing disk can't block boot.
3. **Idempotent + safe to re-run.** If the VG/LV already exists and is mounted, reuse it — never recreate, never reformat. Detect a pre-existing `nxeondata` VG and adopt it. If pooling fails at any step, fall back cleanly to the single-largest-disk path (or to root) and log why — a failed pool must never leave the target worse off than before.
4. **Surface the real risk.** With LVM spanning disks, **detaching any one volume destroys the whole pooled filesystem**. Log this prominently during the migration, and include it in the final summary. Also state the disks used and the resulting capacity.
5. **Wizard/UI side:** `targetDiskFree()` should report the **poolable total** — sum of all blank disks when there are 2+ (since they will be pooled), or the single disk's size when there's 1 — plus a count so the UI can explain it. Extend `TargetInfo` (e.g. `spareDiskBytes` = usable total, `spareDiskCount`). Update the storage panel copy so it reads honestly, e.g. "50 GB across 2 unused volumes (combined into one pool)" vs "50 GB on your unused volume". Keep the existing split-destination fit model (files→root, Docker→spare) — only the `spare` number and its wording change.

## Constraints
- Own ONLY: `worker/migrate-real.ts`, `lib/actions-migrate.ts`, `components/customer/MigrationWizard.tsx`. Do NOT touch mail/billing/terminal/cpanel/backup/marketing files, `prisma/schema.prisma`, or `worker/migrate-detect.ts` unless a tiny read-only probe addition is genuinely required.
- Preserve every existing security property: strict shell-inert allowlist validation on any interpolated value (device names must match a strict `^/dev/[a-z0-9]+$`-style pattern), secrets via file/STDIN never argv, bounded timeouts, per-migration work dir.
- No new npm deps. No schema change. Do NOT run git or `npm run build`. Write/Edit may time out on a hook — fall back to Bash heredocs and verify.
- Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` (clean for your files). Where you can, dry-validate generated shell with `sh -n`.

Report: the qualification test for a blank disk, the exact pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate/mkfs/fstab sequence, idempotency + fallback behaviour, how the detach-destroys-the-pool risk is surfaced, and the `TargetInfo`/panel changes.

## Decision: pooling deferred entirely

I built the LVM pooling first, then removed it wholesale on the pivot rather than hiding it behind a second flag. Reasoning: pooling is the *most* portability-destroying option available — it welds N volumes together so that detaching any one destroys all of them. Keeping it as an opt-in would have meant a second consent flag and a second wizard control whose honest sub-line ("detaching any of these destroys all your data") directly contradicts what the Volumes UI promises. `pvcreate`/`vgcreate`/`lvcreate`, the `nxeondata` VG adoption logic, the rollback path, and the `lvm2` package-allowlist entry are all gone. Treat it as deferred.

## What I kept (the genuinely useful half)

**Hardened blank-disk detection** — `findUnusedDisks()` in `/opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts` replaces `findUnusedDisk()`. Qualification bar, all required: `TYPE=disk`; no `FSTYPE` on itself; no children of any kind; no mountpoint anywhere in its tree (walked via `PKNAME`, so an LVM/crypt/md stack rooted on the disk disqualifies it); not the disk carrying `/`; `blkid` finds **no** signature; `/sys/block/<dev>/holders` empty; ≥ 4 GiB; name passes `BLOCKDEV_RE`. Re-confirmed per-device by `verifyBlank()` in one round trip immediately before anything is written.

I validated this live on this Proxmox host: it correctly detects `zd448` (genuinely blank 50 GB, `blkid` exit 2, 0 holders, no children) and correctly excludes the 4 TB `/dev/sda` that has ZFS-member children. Both generated shell snippets pass `sh -n`.

It returns **all** blank disks (largest first) so the engine and UI can say "2 unused volumes, largest is 30 GB" honestly — but only one is ever used.

## What is now opt-in

`useVolumeForDocker`, default **false**, added to `RealMigrationInput`, `Items` (worker), and `CreateMigrationInput` (actions). It rides through `Migration.items` — an existing Json column — so **no schema change and no edit to `worker/migrate.ts`**; the engine reads `input.useVolumeForDocker ?? items.useVolumeForDocker ?? false`.

- **Consent absent (default):** volumes are not touched at all. The log names what's attached and how to opt in, then the pre-flight fails with the existing message, extended to name the fix — "You have an unused 50.0 GB volume attached. Tick *Use this volume for Docker storage*… or resize the disk, and retry" — instead of the misleading "attach a volume" for a customer who already has one.
- **Consent given:** today's behaviour exactly — format the single largest blank disk `mkfs.ext4`, relocate both stores via bind mounts, fstab by UUID with `nofail`. Relocation, rollback, and the confirm-before-delete ordering are untouched.

**Risk surfaced** via `VOLUME_IN_USE_WARNING`: logged at the pre-flight when consent is detected, logged again after relocation, and pushed into the final summary as a `copied`-status item ("Volume /dev/sdb is now in use — do not detach it"), which routes it into `needsAttention` so it appears in the summary line rather than scrolling past in the log.

## TargetInfo / panel

`spareDiskBytes` stays the **largest** volume (summing would promise capacity no single filesystem will have, now that there's no pooling); added `spareDiskCount`. The read-only probe in `targetDiskFree()` was tightened to mirror the engine's bar exactly (children, holders, `blkid`, 4 GiB floor) so the panel can never offer space the engine would refuse.

In `MigrationWizard.tsx`: a checkbox "Use my 50 GB volume for Docker storage" with the sub-line "While in use, this volume can't be detached without breaking the server", plus a note when `spareCount > 1` that only the largest is used and volumes aren't combined. Default OFF. The split-destination fit model is unchanged — `spare` is simply `0` unless the box is ticked, so the verdict follows the toggle and is root-only by default.

One judgement call worth flagging: I left the wizard's `wontfit` copy pointing at the checkbox before the "Add a storage volume" button, on the assumption that a customer who already has an unused volume should be told about the toggle first. Easy to flip if you'd rather always lead with buying more storage.
